## Walkthrough

This pull request adds an **Access Limit After Unlock** feature that controls how long a blocked domain remains accessible after a successful journal match. The implementation spans documentation, utility functions, service worker state management, settings UI, and popup diagnostics. Core logic includes journal evaluation with TTL caching, cooldown computation, and persistent tracking of blocked attempts and intentional sessions in Chrome local storage. The settings page gains a new numeric field, test button, and weekly attention report showing attempt/session metrics. The popup displays detailed diagnostics across configuration, URL state, journal status, and access decisions.

## Sequence Diagram(s)

No sequence diagrams are generated for this section, as the high-level flows are already captured in the review stack layers above, which provide detailed visualization of journal evaluation, navigation decisions, form validation, and popup initialization.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces several significant features, including an optional access limit after unlocking a domain, a diagnostic popup for real-time status, and a weekly attention report in the settings page. It also refactors journal fetching and adds local storage for tracking blocked attempts and intentional sessions. Feedback highlights a potential race condition in storage updates during concurrent navigations and suggests performance optimizations by caching parsed CSV entries instead of re-parsing them on every navigation.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The `recordBlockedAttempt` function (and others like `recordIntentionalSession` and `markAttemptsJournaledLater`) suffers from a race condition. Since `chrome.storage.local.get` and `set` are asynchronous, multiple concurrent navigations can load the same state, modify it, and then overwrite each other's changes. This can lead to lost data in the "Weekly Attention Report". Consider using a promise-based queue or a locking mechanism to ensure storage updates are performed sequentially.

🟢 **Low** `service-worker.js:48` Multiple concurrent `onBeforeNavigate` events interleave between `loadBlockedAttempts()` and `saveBlockedAttempts()` in `recordBlockedAttempt`, so opening several blocked tabs at once causes later saves to overwrite earlier ones—losing blocked attempt records. Consider acquiring a lock around the read-modify-write sequence, or using `chrome.storage.local` with a single atomic update that appends without reading first.
🚀 Reply "fix it for me" or copy this AI Prompt for your agent: ```text In file service-worker.js around line 48: Multiple concurrent `onBeforeNavigate` events interleave between `loadBlockedAttempts()` and `saveBlockedAttempts()` in `recordBlockedAttempt`, so opening several blocked tabs at once causes later saves to overwrite earlier ones—losing blocked attempt records. Consider acquiring a lock around the read-modify-write sequence, or using `chrome.storage.local` with a single atomic update that appends without reading first. Evidence trail: service-worker.js lines 37-45 (loadBlockedAttempts/saveBlockedAttempts), lines 49-62 (recordBlockedAttempt with read-modify-write), lines 153-185 (async onBeforeNavigate listener calling recordBlockedAttempt without serialization). Reviewed at REVIEWED_COMMIT. ```

**Actionable comments posted: 7**

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for all review comments with AI agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the
rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate.

Inline comments:
In `@popup/popup.js`:
- Around line 32-36: The remaining-time rounding is off in formatExpiry: replace
the Math.ceil-based logic with integer-minute logic so 60–119 seconds shows "1
minute left" (not "less than 1 minute" or "2 minutes"). In function
formatExpiry, compute seconds as before, then set minutes = Math.floor(seconds /
60); if seconds < 60 return `${formatDateTime(expiresAt)} (less than 1 minute
left)`; otherwise return `${formatDateTime(expiresAt)} (${minutes}
minute${minutes !== 1 ? 's' : ''} left)` so boundaries (60s, 61s, etc.) display
correctly.
- Around line 100-129: The popup currently fetches the journal and surfaces
errors even when the page is not blocked; move or short-circuit that logic so
journal fetch is skipped for non-blocked URLs: check matchedPattern immediately
and call setSummary('allowed', 'URL is not blocked', ...) and
setDiagnostic('accessStatus','Allowed') then return before calling
fetchJournalCachedResult, evaluateJournalAccess,
loadIntentionalSessionsForPopup, findIntentionalSession, or
evaluateUnlockCooldown; alternatively, wrap the fetch/error branch to ignore
failures when matchedPattern is false and keep accessStatus neutral/Allowed
instead of setting a blocked summary.

In `@service-worker-utils.js`:
- Around line 60-84: The cache currently only stores successful fetches; change
the logic in the function that calls fetchJournal (references: journalCache,
fetchJournal, journalUrl, CACHE_TTL_MS, now) to always populate journalCache
with the result (set url, status, text, error, fetchedAt: now) regardless of
result.ok, then in the cached-return branch return the cached object's actual
ok/status/text/error values (and fromCache: true); keep the existing behavior of
updating the cache on each fetch and returning { ...result, fromCache: false }
when not using cache.

In `@service-worker.js`:
- Around line 36-45: The current loadBlockedAttempts/saveBlockedAttempts pair
allows race conditions by letting callers perform independent read-modify-write
cycles; replace them with a serialized update API (e.g., a single
updateBlockedAttempts(fn) or an internal mutex/queue) that loads the array,
applies a synchronous updater function, truncates to MAX_BLOCKED_ATTEMPTS, and
writes back before allowing the next update; update callers
(recordBlockedAttempt, markAttemptsJournaledLater, recordIntentionalSession) to
call this serialized helper instead of calling
loadBlockedAttempts/saveBlockedAttempts directly so concurrent navigations
cannot overwrite each other.

In `@settings/settings.js`:
- Around line 153-175: The loadWeeklyReport function lacks error handling: wrap
the await chrome.storage.local.get and renderWeeklyReport call in a try/catch
(inside loadWeeklyReport), catch any errors from storage access or rendering,
log the error (console.error) and surface user feedback (e.g., enable refresh
button and call a new or existing UI error renderer like renderWeeklyReportError
or set text on the refresh/report container) while still ensuring the refresh
button is re-enabled in the finally block; reference loadWeeklyReport,
renderWeeklyReport, BLOCKED_ATTEMPTS_STORAGE_KEY and
INTENTIONAL_SESSIONS_STORAGE_KEY to locate the code to modify.
- Line 7: The assignment for timeframeMinutes uses parseInt on
document.getElementById('timeframe').value but allows negative or zero values;
update the code that computes timeframeMinutes so it parses the value
(parseInt(..., 10)), verifies it's a finite positive integer (>= 1), and if not
clamped or fallback to 60; locate the expression referencing timeframeMinutes
and document.getElementById('timeframe').value and replace it with logic that
enforces min 1 and defaults to 60 when parseInt returns NaN or a value < 1.
- Around line 109-119: In summarizeSessionsByDomain, guard against malformed
session records by skipping or normalizing entries with missing/non-string
domain and non-numeric visitCount before aggregating and sorting: ensure when
iterating sessions you only use session.domain if it exists and is a string (or
coerce to a safe string key) and treat session.visitCount as a number (default
to 1), and in the final sort compare fallback keys (e.g., empty string) so
localeCompare never receives undefined; update the aggregation logic (summary
map usage in summarizeSessionsByDomain) and the sort comparator to use these
safe values.
```

</details>

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Validate `timeframeMinutes` as a positive integer.**

On **Line 7**, negative values are accepted (`parseInt('-30', 10)`), which can make test outcomes misleading. Clamp to `>= 1` with a default fallback.

 

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-    timeframeMinutes: parseInt(document.getElementById('timeframe').value, 10) || 60,
+    timeframeMinutes: Math.max(1, parseInt(document.getElementById('timeframe').value, 10) || 60),
```
</details>
